subject: Re: Segmented discount tiers for renewal + midcycle top-up

From: Diane Holt <diane.holt@luminadx.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Wells <ethan@luminadx.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing for expansion

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. We are preparing a mid-cycle expansion request (additional seats and more throughput) and our procurement team asked for two things before we proceed:

- A clear proration approach if we add capacity mid-quarter
- An updated discount schedule if we increase committed units (we typically look for stepped discounts at $X, $Y thresholds)

Can you share an example of how Redwood would structure a renewal+top-up for a customer moving from a 4 GPU reserved commit to an 8 GPU commit mid-term? Also happy to hop on a short call — Ethan and I are free Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Diane
Director, Infrastructure
Lumina Diagnostics

--

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Diane Holt <diane.holt@luminadx.com>
Cc: Ethan Wells <ethan@luminadx.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing for expansion

Hi Diane — great to hear. Short answer: we can do a midterm top-up with pro-rated billing plus a segmented discount schedule that preserves the customer’s effective unit price while rewarding larger committed bands.

I attached a sample layout (segmented_pricing_v2.xlsx) that shows:
- how proration works for partial months
- three discount bands (Tier A: baseline, Tier B: +20% commit, Tier C: +50% commit) with blended effective pricing
- an optional one-time voucher to offset transition costs (usable on month one only)

If it helps, we can present two options:
1) Fast path: immediate 8-GPU top-up, prorated for the remainder of the term, with a small one-time voucher (5% ARR credit)
2) Co-term path: annualize to a new 12-month commit starting on the next billing cycle with deeper discounts in Tiers B/C

Would Laura and Marissa be able to join a 30-min call Thursday at 10:30am PT? I’ll put together the numbers if you confirm.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick operational notes from finance/ops POV ahead of the call:

- Voucher mechanics: one-time invoice credit applied on first invoice post-change; not refundable and cannot be applied against past due balances. We’ll include language in the amendment.
- Proration: we apply a daily proration for GPU reserved capacity; example in the sheet uses 30-day month for simplicity but ops will compute by actual days.
- Co-term pro-forma: Laura (me) will produce a sample pro-forma for Year 1 reflecting both the fast path and co-term path (line items: base commit, added capacity, voucher credit, taxes).

Marissa — can you prepare the pro-forma (two columns: Fast path vs Co-term) and a short explanation of when co-term gives better ARR leverage? Vivek — please confirm discount floor we can offer for Tier C (I recommend not below 18% effective).

Talk at 10:30.

Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Recap:

- Finance confirmed voucher is a non-refundable invoice credit applied to the first post-change invoice.
- Ops will produce a Day-accurate pro-forma for Year 1 for both options by Monday.

3) Vivek: confirm final floor on Tier C discount (callout: 18% effective floor) and any escalation path if Lumina pushes lower.

I’ll send a clean amendment draft once we get Lumina’s selection. Thanks again — appreciate the pragmatic conversation.

Best,
